Subject: Bridgeport security questionnaire: data residency & retention (hosted API)

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Bridgeport's security team has a short follow-up on hosted API data handling so we can finish our Risk Assessment. The attachment is our condensed questionnaire (Section A). Can you confirm the items below for hosted API customers?

1) Where is customer data stored by default (region & cloud provider)?
2) What is the default retention period for user-provided payloads, request logs, and model artifacts?
3) What is the documented process and SLA for permanent deletion / data cessation (including backups)?
4) Do you provide an option to opt out of request retention for debugging/telemetry? If so, how is it configured?

We appreciate short, point-form answers and any evidence links you can attach.

Attaching: Bridgeport_SQ_v3.pdf

Best,
Elena Suarez
Security Program Manager
Bridgeport AI

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@bridgeport.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-18T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Bridgeport security questionnaire: data residency & retention (hosted API)

Elena — thanks for the questions. Answers below (concise, with evidence links and an attachment we referenced in the call). If you want a one-page excerpt for your assessment report I can distill this further.

1) Default storage location:
- Hosted API default region: customers are served from the nearest available region; primary regions we offer today are us-west-2 (AWS) and eu-west-1 (AWS).
- Default tenancy: multi-tenant by default; enterprise customers may request Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC) to isolate compute and storage.
- Data in transit and at rest is TLS 1.2+/AES-256 encrypted; keys are managed via our KMS (customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private).

2) Default retention periods (hosted API):
- Request payloads (customer inputs and outputs): retained 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring.
- Request logs and traces (routing/latency metadata): retained 45 days.
- Model artifacts (weights, checkpoints): immutable versions we store for serving are retained per our internal model retention policy (retention of model binaries is operational and not customer-request-specific).
- Cache/KV ephemeral state: kept only for the duration needed to serve the request (evicted per session/TTL, typically seconds-to-minutes), not persisted beyond the configured TTL.

3) Deletion / data cessation process & SLAs:
- Customer-initiated erasure: we provide an API endpoint and a Support flow. On receipt of a verified erasure request (via console or support ticket), we:
  a) schedule immediate logical deletion of tenant-associated request payloads and derived artifacts within 72 hours;
  b) begin deletion from primary stores and remove indexing metadata to make data non-retrievable;
  c) cascade deletion to analytics/telemetry stores within 7 days.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are retained up to 90 days for disaster recovery. Backups are subject to a secure rotation and purge pipeline; when an erasure request affects customer data we mark those objects for redaction from backups and execute purging as part of the next backup lifecycle (maximum 90-day bound).
- Audit & attestation: deletion actions generate audit entries (who/when/method) visible to Support and recorded in our internal SIEM. For enterprise contracts we provide an erasure certificate once the pipeline confirms completion.

4) Opt-out of request retention:
- Yes. Customers can opt out of request retention via:
  a) Console toggle for "No Request Retention" which suppresses storage of full request/response payloads (still logs minimal telemetry for billing/rate limits); or
  b) API flag at request time: include header X-Redwood-Retention: none to indicate ephemeral-only handling.
- When opt-out is enabled: payloads are processed in-memory, not written to persistent storage. Short-term runtime caches may still exist but are TTL-limited and never written to long-term stores.

Evidence & attachments:
- Attached: redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (high-level flow showing customer ingress, GPU serving tier, cache, and archive path).
- Evidence link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Bridgeport/SQ-evidence (contains SOC-2 control mappings and sample erasure certificate).
- We also attached retention_policy_summary.pdf for your team to reference.

Notes / caveats:
- Different contracted plans (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) have different default retention and residency controls — the answers above are for the standard Hosted API offering.
- If Bridgeport needs region lock (data pinned to us-west-2) we can add a region constraint to the account with an SLA change.

If you want we can schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up to walk an engineer through the deletion pipeline and show audit entries.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_data_flow_diagram.png, retention_policy_summary.pdf
